comments.body:
Thanks, Alex. Replacing the retired default makes sense. Before merging, could you also address a request-format issue that predates this PR? Otherwise, updating the model name alone will still leave the generation path broken.

In `GeminiImageProvider._prepare_api_request()`, `aspectRatio`, `imageSize`, `numberOfImages`, and `personGeneration` are currently placed directly under `generationConfig`. I checked the [official v1beta Discovery schema](https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/$discovery/rest?version=v1beta):
- `aspectRatio` and `imageSize` belong inside `generationConfig.imageConfig`.
- `numberOfImages` and `personGeneration` are not supported fields there and should be removed. Please also handle `num_images > 1` explicitly, either through supported batch orchestration or a clear validation error, rather than silently ignoring the requested count.

The new default-value tests are useful, but they don't exercise the outgoing request. Could you add a mocked `generate()` test that checks the JSON structure and processes a successful image response? Keeping the default-consistency checks alongside that would give us much better coverage.

Could you also confirm that `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` supports the existing `generateContent` endpoint? Google's current guide emphasizes Interactions; that alone doesn't mean `generateContent` is unsupported, but we haven't verified this model/endpoint combination with a live key. If you have access, a brief redacted smoke-test result—model/endpoint, HTTP status, and whether a final image was returned—would help. Please don't include keys or authorization headers. If a live test isn't available, please document that limitation and provide an authoritative compatibility reference.

One smaller point: the renamed model entry still advertises `max_resolution: 1024x1024`. Please check that it reflects the provider's implemented resolution support.

The build and all four browser CI shards passed, and I ran 16 related tests successfully. No paid live image request was made during the review. Thanks for taking a look at these remaining gaps.

Pushed a commit addressing the review:

- `_prepare_api_request()` now sends `aspectRatio` and `imageSize` inside `generationConfig.imageConfig`; `numberOfImages` and `personGeneration` are removed.
- `num_images > 1` returns an explicit `unsupported_num_images` error without calling the API (generateContent returns one image per call and the provider only read the first before).
- New mocked `generate()` test checks the outgoing URL/JSON and processes a successful `inlineData` image response; the default-consistency tests are kept.
- The listed `max_resolution` is now `2048x2048`, matching the 2K tier `_map_image_size()` requests for longest sides >= 1400 px.

On `generateContent`: no live Gemini key was available, so there is no smoke-test result for `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` on that endpoint. Google's [model page](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-nano-banana-2.1) lists image generation and 1K/2K/4K output sizes for this model. The current [image generation guide](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation) only shows the Interactions API (`/v1beta/interactions`); neither page says whether `generateContent` is supported for it. The request shape now follows the v1beta `GenerationConfig.imageConfig` schema you linked. If you would rather not rely on that, I can move this provider to the Interactions API in this PR.


This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
